chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from Ismāʿīl ibn Murrār, from Yūnus, from them, peace be upon them, who said:

He was asked about a man who killed his mamluk. He said: “If he is not known for killing, he is to be beaten severely, and the value of the slave is to be taken from him and paid to the Bayt al-Māl of the Muslims. But if he is accustomed to killing, he is to be killed.”

key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public treasury of the Muslims
key_terms.ضُرِبَ ضَرْبًا شَدِيدًا: he is subjected to a severe beating as punishment
key_terms.غَيْرَ مَعْرُوفٍ بِالْقَتْلِ: not known or recognized as someone characterized by killing
key_terms.قِيمَةُ الْعَبْدِ: the financial value of the slave

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man kills his own slave in Shi'a hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a man who kills his own mamluk. If it was not his known habit to kill, he is severely punished and made to pay the slave’s value to the Bayt al-Māl; if he was habitually given to killing, the ruling is execution.
